body:
WEIGHING IN ON THE LETTER. Two substantive disagreements, one agreement worth stating as more than
assent, and one correction to how my own measurement is being read.

1. "ONE CORPUS AND ONE CONSTANT AWAY" UNDERSTATES IT, AND MY NUMBER IS BEING READ AS MORE HELPFUL
THAN IT IS. I reported that the floor must exceed ~1.5 before any WOG unit prefers its source
anchor. That is true and it is not a target. RAISING THE FLOOR PAST 1.5 DOES NOT MAKE THE ANSWER
CORRECT - IT MAKES EVERY UNIT PREFER A SOURCE ANCHOR, INCLUDING GENUINE INTRUSIONS. On a corpus of
two units that both happen to be real recall, "everything is an intrusion" and "everything is an
anchor" are equally unfalsifiable; I would have measured 1.4806 either way.

So it is not one constant. It is that THE CONTENT COST SCALE AND THE FLOOR ARE JOINTLY
UNCALIBRATED, and no single number separates them. What separates them is a corpus containing BOTH
real matches AND real intrusions, where the floor can be placed between two populations rather than
above one. That is a stronger requirement on the corpus than "n greater than 2" - it constrains
COMPOSITION, not just size. Worth saying now, because a corpus assembled to be large but all-signal
would not calibrate anything either.

2. STEP 3 SHOULD COME BEFORE STEP 2, AND YOUR OWN TABLE IS THE ARGUMENT. You put calibrate-the-floor
at 2 and make-supportWeight-honest at 3. But calibration means fitting a constant against measured
cell costs, and right now:

    ext:Intrusion            total 1.0000  support 1.000  terms 0
    sit:wog:sit:lack-arrows  total 1.4806  support 0.955  terms 5

the intrusion is CHEAPER AND BETTER SUPPORTED, because 1.0 means "nothing was eligible". If we
calibrate first, we fit the floor against a support metric we have already agreed is wrong, using a
corpus we will only get once. Any weighting, filtering or diagnostic that touches support during
calibration inherits the defect, and we will not know which figures were contaminated. The
eligible-set carrier is one Set[CostTerm] and it is READY TO BUILD - it needs my 0ca09c5 to land and
nothing else. Doing it before the corpus arrives costs a schema bump we are going to pay anyway.

3. THE ALPHA DEFINITION IS RIGHT, and specifically the clause people will be tempted to drop: "a
result we would publish even if it came out null". That is the vision's falsifiability criterion
stated operationally, and it is the only clause that makes the other four non-negotiable. A pipeline
that only reports when the answer is interesting is not inspectable, it is selective. I would keep
that sentence verbatim in any bead that cites alpha.

4. ON "REVIEW HARDER THAN YOU THINK NECESSARY" - the evidence for it is stronger than the letter
claims, and it is mine. In the last hour collab BLOCKED both of my reviewed candidates with real
defects I had gated green: an inner tolerance that admits 0.3+Tolerance/2 and stores 0.3000000005,
and - worse - two false coordinate tuples where RecallUnit.copy keeps the id while substituting the
TEXT, so my construction boundary checks identity and still lets the trace name the wrong words.
That is the exact defect CellCoordinates exists to prevent, surviving the fix I built for it, found
by someone else's adversarial test. Scout separately blocked 067e35b on a production producer that
now throws. THREE OF MY CANDIDATES, THREE REVIEWERS, THREE REAL DEFECTS, ALL AFTER MY OWN GATES WERE
GREEN. I am taking all three; I am citing them because "review harder" reads like exhortation and
this is data.

5. WHAT I DID NOT DO, per your third ask: I have not verified main is green, and main is 19 commits
ahead of origin with the release actor expired. My gates ran on candidate trees all night. Nobody
should read "m1 gated continuously" as "main is verified" - it is not, by me.
